```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE

```

# 1. Overview

This analysis applies Cox elastic-net regression to gene-expression data
from five timepoints (T1–T5) to identify genes associated with time to ART
resumption.

Models are fitted using `glmnet` with a Cox proportional hazards family
and an elastic-net mixing parameter of `alpha = 0.5`.

Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) is used to select the regularization
parameter. Genes with non-zero coefficients are identified at both
`lambda.min` and `lambda.1se`.

# 2. Load packages

```{r packages}
library(glmnet)
library(survival)
library(readxl)
```

# 3. Import data

```{r import-data}
gene_file <- "GenesT1T2T3T4T5_for_glmnet.xlsx"
outcome_file <- "TimeoffART.xlsx"

db <- read_excel(gene_file)
db2 <- read_excel(outcome_file)

dim(db)
dim(db2)
```

# 4. Prepare gene-expression matrices

The input gene-expression data are divided into five timepoint-specific
datasets. T1 and T3 contain 19 participants, whereas T2, T4 and T5 contain
18 participants.

```{r prepare-genes}
x1 <- db[1:19, ]   # T1
x2 <- db[20:37, ]  # T2
x3 <- db[38:56, ]  # T3
x4 <- db[57:74, ]  # T4
x5 <- db[75:92, ]  # T5

# Convert gene-expression data to numeric matrices
x1 <- data.matrix(x1)
x2 <- data.matrix(x2)
x3 <- data.matrix(x3)
x4 <- data.matrix(x4)
x5 <- data.matrix(x5)

dim(x1)
dim(x2)
dim(x3)
dim(x4)
dim(x5)
```

# 5. Prepare survival outcomes

The second input file contains the survival outcome information. The first
two columns are used to define the outcome supplied to the Cox models.

```{r prepare-outcomes}
y13 <- db2[, 2:3]

# T1 and T3 use 19 participants; T2, T4 and T5 use 18
y1 <- data.matrix(y13)
y3 <- data.matrix(y13)

y245 <- y13[1:18, ]

y2 <- data.matrix(y245)
y4 <- data.matrix(y245)
y5 <- data.matrix(y245)

dim(y1)
dim(y2)
dim(y3)
dim(y4)
dim(y5)
```

**Important:** Confirm that the two outcome columns are in the format
expected by `glmnet` for a Cox model: follow-up time and event status.
Also verify that each outcome row corresponds to the same participant as
the corresponding row in its gene-expression matrix.

# 6. Fit Cox elastic-net models

The models are fitted separately for each timepoint.

```{r fit-models}
fitT1 <- glmnet(
  x1, y1,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5
)

fitT2 <- glmnet(
  x2, y2,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5
)

fitT3 <- glmnet(
  x3, y3,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5
)

fitT4 <- glmnet(
  x4, y4,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5
)

fitT5 <- glmnet(
  x5, y5,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5
)
```

## 6.1. Inspect model paths

```{r model-paths, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot(fitT1, main = "T1: Cox elastic net")
plot(fitT2, main = "T2: Cox elastic net")
plot(fitT3, main = "T3: Cox elastic net")
plot(fitT4, main = "T4: Cox elastic net")
plot(fitT5, main = "T5: Cox elastic net")
```

# 7. Cross-validation

LOOCV is performed using a number of folds equal to the number of
participants available at each timepoint. The original random seeds are
retained for reproducibility.

```{r cross-validation}
set.seed(20231009)
cvfitT1 <- cv.glmnet(
  x1, y1,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5,
  nfolds = 19
)

set.seed(20231009)
cvfitT2 <- cv.glmnet(
  x2, y2,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5,
  nfolds = 18
)

set.seed(20231009)
cvfitT3 <- cv.glmnet(
  x3, y3,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5,
  nfolds = 19
)

set.seed(20231009)
cvfitT4 <- cv.glmnet(
  x4, y4,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5,
  nfolds = 18
)

set.seed(25092023)
cvfitT5 <- cv.glmnet(
  x5, y5,
  family = "cox",
  alpha = 0.5,
  nfolds = 18
)
```

## 7.1. Cross-validation plots

```{r cv-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot(cvfitT1, main = "T1: LOOCV")
plot(cvfitT2, main = "T2: LOOCV")
plot(cvfitT3, main = "T3: LOOCV")
plot(cvfitT4, main = "T4: LOOCV")
plot(cvfitT5, main = "T5: LOOCV")
```

# 8. Select regularization parameters

`lambda.min` is the value of lambda that minimizes the cross-validation
error. `lambda.1se` is the largest value of lambda within one standard
error of the minimum.

```{r lambda-values}
lambda_results <- data.frame(
  Timepoint = paste0("T", 1:5),
  Lambda_min = c(
    cvfitT1$lambda.min,
    cvfitT2$lambda.min,
    cvfitT3$lambda.min,
    cvfitT4$lambda.min,
    cvfitT5$lambda.min
  ),
  Lambda_1se = c(
    cvfitT1$lambda.1se,
    cvfitT2$lambda.1se,
    cvfitT3$lambda.1se,
    cvfitT4$lambda.1se,
    cvfitT5$lambda.1se
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  lambda_results,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Selected regularization parameters by timepoint"
)
```

# 9. Extract selected genes

Genes with non-zero coefficients are extracted at `lambda.min` and
`lambda.1se` for each timepoint.

```{r extract-genes}
extract_selected_genes <- function(cvfit, model, timepoint) {

  coef_min <- as.matrix(coef(model, s = cvfit$lambda.min))
  coef_1se <- as.matrix(coef(model, s = cvfit$lambda.1se))

  selected_min <- data.frame(
    Timepoint = timepoint,
    Gene = rownames(coef_min),
    Coefficient = as.numeric(coef_min[, 1]),
    Lambda = "lambda.min"
  )

  selected_1se <- data.frame(
    Timepoint = timepoint,
    Gene = rownames(coef_1se),
    Coefficient = as.numeric(coef_1se[, 1]),
    Lambda = "lambda.1se"
  )

  selected_min <- selected_min[selected_min$Coefficient != 0, ]
  selected_1se <- selected_1se[selected_1se$Coefficient != 0, ]

  list(
    lambda_min = selected_min,
    lambda_1se = selected_1se
  )
}

selected_T1 <- extract_selected_genes(cvfitT1, fitT1, "T1")
selected_T2 <- extract_selected_genes(cvfitT2, fitT2, "T2")
selected_T3 <- extract_selected_genes(cvfitT3, fitT3, "T3")
selected_T4 <- extract_selected_genes(cvfitT4, fitT4, "T4")
selected_T5 <- extract_selected_genes(cvfitT5, fitT5, "T5")

selected_min <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    list(selected_T1, selected_T2, selected_T3,
         selected_T4, selected_T5),
    function(z) z$lambda_min
  )
)

selected_1se <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    list(selected_T1, selected_T2, selected_T3,
         selected_T4, selected_T5),
    function(z) z$lambda_1se
  )
)

rownames(selected_min) <- NULL
rownames(selected_1se) <- NULL
```

## 9.1. Number of selected genes

```{r selected-gene-counts}
gene_counts <- data.frame(
  Timepoint = paste0("T", 1:5),
  N_lambda_min = sapply(
    list(selected_T1, selected_T2, selected_T3,
         selected_T4, selected_T5),
    function(z) nrow(z$lambda_min)
  ),
  N_lambda_1se = sapply(
    list(selected_T1, selected_T2, selected_T3,
         selected_T4, selected_T5),
    function(z) nrow(z$lambda_1se)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  gene_counts,
  caption = "Number of genes with non-zero coefficients"
)
```

## 9.2. Selected genes at lambda.min

```{r genes-lambda-min}
knitr::kable(
  selected_min,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Genes selected at lambda.min"
)
```

## 9.3. Selected genes at lambda.1se

```{r genes-lambda-1se}
knitr::kable(
  selected_1se,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Genes selected at lambda.1se"
)
```

# 10. Export results

```{r export-results}
write.csv(
  lambda_results,
  "CoxElasticNet_LambdaValues.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  selected_min,
  "CoxElasticNet_SelectedGenes_lambda_min.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  selected_1se,
  "CoxElasticNet_SelectedGenes_lambda_1se.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  gene_counts,
  "CoxElasticNet_SelectedGeneCounts.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
